payload.assumptions_validated:
KILLER. Three ranked unknowns, three spikes, three answers - and only ONE came back the way I hoped, which is the point of ranking them by what would hurt most.

U1 THE PARSE (highest, because it could still overturn the architecture) - HOLDS. run-220f463e2243: em-dashes preserved, recovered text BYTE-IDENTICAL to the file's own line, text containing colons parsing cleanly, 0 malformed records across every case. FLIP 1 does not fire; the git-only winner stands on evidence rather than on a five-point margin. Two contract findings came free and go straight into the build: exit 1 means NO MATCHES with empty stdout (must map to 'no matches', never to an error), exit 128 means a real failure such as a bad ref - and those two being DISTINGUISHABLE is what stops a typo'd ref reading as 'nothing found'. Scale measured at 1314 matches across 456 files uncapped, which confirms R28's caps by measurement.

U2 SEMANTIC SELECTION - DOES NOT HOLD, and candidate X2 is ELIMINATED ON EVIDENCE rather than on my prior. Querying the ledger index with a machine state's own statement returned exactly one hit: the state node itself. It did NOT return meth-state-of-the-art, the rule that demonstrably binds that state. The index is fine - a direct query for 'state-of-the-art scan' finds that node - the JOIN is wrong, because rules are written in general vocabulary and states in specific vocabulary, and the overlap is near zero. It would have returned a plausible set while missing the binding rule, with nothing at the point of use showing the miss. That is exactly the failure C7 was written to catch, now measured.

U3 CAN A LINT SEE THE ALLOCATION - DOES NOT HOLD, AND THE DESIGN CHANGED. Measured: zero element or design nodes in the ledger, the allocation living only as prose inside evidence JSON, and one solitary `design:` marker across the engine. The models-adhered lint - this iteration's flagship, the check that would have caught i8d's escaped defects - cannot be built. AND IT GENERALIZES: my own 29-requirement register is one prose string in one field, so every lint over requirement fields or tracing is equally impossible. The process produces PROSE where a lint needs DATA.

SO THE DESIGN CHANGED RATHER THAN THE CLAIM BEING SOFTENED: the lint set shrinks to facts that exist outside prose - run records, git facts, evidence-field presence, grant shape, guidance volume, log facts. Story S2's second slide was rewritten to match. R16 survives with a smaller set. The prerequisite is recorded as se.raid-items-are-prose-so-the-best-checks-cannot-be-mechanical, owner-owned, because ITEMS-BECOME-NODES is a spec-structure iteration and taking it here would double this one.

I would rather report a flagship deliverable as blocked at M5 than discover it at M7 - and I note that this is the check i8d skipped, when 'the design document says it was built and verified' went untested until the owner's thumb found it.
payload.buildable:
YES, and the scope is now honest rather than optimistic.

PROVEN, not estimated: the search core is SP1's parse function plus the exit-code contract, exercised against real content on this machine. Ref reads, tag search and v1 search were all exercised at M3. The record work - annotated tags, evidence_commit, branch deletion - is ordinary git against surfaces we own, and its two motivating facts were observed rather than assumed. se_config, batch patching and required-arg enforcement are ordinary engineering with no unknown left in them.

BUILDABLE WITH A SMALLER PROMISE: the lint registry, the verdict block and the decide-or-defer contract all build exactly as designed - what shrinks is the LIST of lints that can be populated today. That is a content limit, not a structural one, which matters: when items become nodes, the registry accepts the new lints without redesign.

NO NEW ELEMENT was needed during probing, so nothing returns to the architecture gate. The one I predicted might appear - a migration helper for the applies_to rewrite - is still expected, and it is a build step inside E5 rather than a ninth element.

WHAT IS NOT BUILDABLE AND IS NOT PRETENDED TO BE: conformance-to-allocation, requirement-field coverage, trace completeness. Each blocked on the same prerequisite, each recorded, none quietly dropped.
payload.results_recorded:
Every spike pinned to its run; nothing retyped from memory.

SP1 -> run-220f463e2243 (and its failed first attempt, run-32dae1ec840a, which is worth keeping: the harness crashed because git grep exits 1 on no-match, so the spike's own bug DISCOVERED finding F before the test for it ran).
SP2 -> the se_get_search call above; a code-reading and index-query result rather than an executed script, and recorded as such rather than dressed as an experiment.
SP3 -> run-371f33c5602a, three measurements: zero element nodes, allocation only in evidence prose, one design marker across the engine.

PROMOTIONS MARKED, all permanent rather than provisional: SP1's three-field NUL parse with the ref-prefix strip enters E1 in substance unchanged; the exit-code contract enters as a FACT (0 hits / 1 no-matches / 128 error); four negative cases become permanent tests - no-match is not an error, a bad ref IS an error, colon-bearing text parses, and recovered text is byte-identical to the file - that last one being the guard on the entire git-only decision; and the measured 1314-match pattern becomes the cap test's fixture rather than a synthetic one.

NOT PROMOTED, deliberately: the semantic-join path (eliminated on evidence) and every conformance lint (blocked on the prerequisite).

ONE HONEST GAP IN MY OWN TESTING, stated rather than buried: SP1's long-line case was meant to exercise the design document's enormous lines and the longest it actually hit was 74 characters. Long-line parsing is therefore UNPROVEN. It is a parse-shape question rather than a design question, so it becomes a build-time test instead of a reopened decision - but it is not evidence, and I am not counting it as any.
